summary.thesis: 文章的核心不是“让 Agent 多写代码”，而是把软件工程系统改造成 Agent 能理解、验证、修复和持续改进的运行环境。
summary.lead: OpenAI 团队刻意采用“0 行人工手写代码”的约束：人类负责设定目标、表达验收标准和编码判断力，Codex 负责执行、审查、修复和合并。这个实验显示，Agent-first 工程的稀缺资源是人类注意力，因此系统必须把 UI、日志、指标、文档、架构规则和质量标准变成 Agent 可直接读取和执行的形式。

keyPoints.label: 要点 1
keyPoints.text: 工程师的主要工作转为设计 harness：工具、脚手架、约束、文档和反馈回路。

keyPoints.label: 要点 2
keyPoints.text: AGENTS.md 不应成为巨型说明书，而应成为通向仓库内知识系统的目录。

keyPoints.label: 要点 3
keyPoints.text: 架构约束、结构测试、自定义 lint 和错误信息共同构成可执行的“品味”。

keyPoints.label: 要点 4
keyPoints.text: 当吞吐量远高于人类评审能力时，合并哲学会转向短 PR、低等待成本和持续修复。

cards.title: 从空仓库到百万行代码
cards.body: 文章从一个强约束实验开始：从空 Git 仓库出发，五个月内由 Codex 生成约百万行代码、合并约 1,500 个 PR，并支撑真实内部用户。重点不是炫耀代码量，而是观察当“人类不再亲自写代码”时，工程系统需要怎样变化。

cards.title: 工程师角色转向 harness 设计
cards.body: 人的工作从实现细节上移到系统设计：拆任务、补工具、写可执行规则、把反馈做成循环。失败被视为系统能力缺口，而不是一次提示词不够用力。

cards.title: 让应用对 Agent 可读
cards.body: 随着代码吞吐提升，瓶颈变成人类 QA。OpenAI 的做法是把浏览器、DOM、截图、日志、指标和 tracing 暴露给 Codex，使 Agent 能在隔离 worktree 中启动应用、复现问题并验证修复。

cards.title: 仓库知识成为记录系统
cards.body: 文章反对把所有规则塞进一个巨大的 AGENTS.md。更有效的方式是让 AGENTS.md 成为地图，真正的知识沉淀在仓库内的 docs、plans、architecture、quality 和 generated schema 中，并通过 lint/CI 维护新鲜度。

cards.title: 架构和品味需要机械化
cards.body: Agent-first 代码库不能只靠文档保持一致性。OpenAI 把依赖方向、领域分层、日志结构、命名、文件大小和平台可靠性做成可检查规则，并把错误信息写成 Agent 可直接执行的修复说明。

cards.title: 吞吐量改变合并策略
cards.body: 当 Agent 的产出速度超过人类注意力，传统“长时间阻塞合并”的策略会变得昂贵。文章强调短 PR、少阻塞门和后续快速修复；这只有在自动化验证和持续清理能力足够强时才成立。

sections.toc: 从空仓库到百万行代码
sections.title: 从空仓库到百万行代码

rows.en: OpenAI describes an internal beta built over five months with zero manually-written code. Codex generated application logic, tests, CI, documentation, observability, and tooling, while humans steered intent and acceptance criteria.
rows.zh: 文章从一个强约束实验开始：从空 Git 仓库出发，五个月内由 Codex 生成约百万行代码、合并约 1,500 个 PR，并支撑真实内部用户。重点不是炫耀代码量，而是观察当“人类不再亲自写代码”时，工程系统需要怎样变化。

sections.toc: 工程师角色转向 harness 设计
sections.title: 工程师角色转向 harness 设计

rows.en: When progress stalled, the answer was not to ask Codex to try harder, but to identify missing capabilities and make them legible and enforceable for the agent.
rows.zh: 人的工作从实现细节上移到系统设计：拆任务、补工具、写可执行规则、把反馈做成循环。失败被视为系统能力缺口，而不是一次提示词不够用力。

sections.toc: 让应用对 Agent 可读
sections.title: 让应用对 Agent 可读

rows.en: The team made UI, logs, metrics, traces, worktrees, browser automation, and observability directly available to Codex so it could reproduce bugs and validate fixes.
rows.zh: 随着代码吞吐提升，瓶颈变成人类 QA。OpenAI 的做法是把浏览器、DOM、截图、日志、指标和 tracing 暴露给 Codex，使 Agent 能在隔离 worktree 中启动应用、复现问题并验证修复。

sections.toc: 仓库知识成为记录系统
sections.title: 仓库知识成为记录系统

rows.en: A short AGENTS.md acts as a table of contents, while structured docs, architecture notes, plans, product specs, generated schemas, and quality documents become the system of record.
rows.zh: 文章反对把所有规则塞进一个巨大的 AGENTS.md。更有效的方式是让 AGENTS.md 成为地图，真正的知识沉淀在仓库内的 docs、plans、architecture、quality 和 generated schema 中，并通过 lint/CI 维护新鲜度。

sections.toc: 架构和品味需要机械化
sections.title: 架构和品味需要机械化

rows.en: The codebase uses rigid layer boundaries, custom linters, structural tests, naming rules, file-size limits, and remediation-oriented error messages to keep agent-generated code coherent.
rows.zh: Agent-first 代码库不能只靠文档保持一致性。OpenAI 把依赖方向、领域分层、日志结构、命名、文件大小和平台可靠性做成可检查规则，并把错误信息写成 Agent 可直接执行的修复说明。

rows.en: With high agent throughput, short-lived PRs and low merge friction can outperform slow blocking gates, because correction is cheap and waiting is expensive.
rows.zh: 当 Agent 的产出速度超过人类注意力，传统“长时间阻塞合并”的策略会变得昂贵。文章强调短 PR、少阻塞门和后续快速修复；这只有在自动化验证和持续清理能力足够强时才成立。

sections.toc: 自主性来自被编码的开发环节
sections.title: 自主性来自被编码的开发环节

rows.en: Codex can now verify state, reproduce bugs, record failing demos, implement fixes, validate them, open PRs, respond to feedback, repair builds, and merge when judgment is not required.
rows.zh: OpenAI 把测试、复现、视频记录、PR 创建、反馈处理、构建修复和人工交接都纳入系统，使 Codex 能端到端完成新功能。文章也明确提醒：这种能力高度依赖仓库结构和工具投入，不能简单泛化。

rows.en: The team moved from weekly manual cleanup to encoded golden principles and recurring Codex background tasks that scan drift, update quality scores, and open targeted refactor PRs.
rows.zh: 完全自主的 Agent 会复制既有模式，也会复制坏模式。OpenAI 把“黄金原则”写成规则，并用后台 Codex 任务持续扫描漂移、更新质量等级、发起重构 PR，让技术债像垃圾回收一样小步清理。

groupDesc.B1: 入门进阶 · 技术文章高频词
groupDesc.B2: 中级 · 工程与产品语境常用
groupDesc.C1: 高级 · 抽象论证与系统设计词汇
groupDesc.C2: 精通 · 高阶表达与隐喻用法
groupDesc.术语: 文章相关专有名词 · Agent / 工程系统

leverage.def: 利用杠杆效应；借助某物放大产出或影响。
leverage.eg: The team used Codex to leverage scarce human attention.
leverage.egzh: 团队用 Codex 放大稀缺的人类注意力。

internal_beta.def: 面向组织内部用户开放的早期测试版本。
internal_beta.eg: The product began as an internal beta.
internal_beta.egzh: 这个产品最初是内部 beta。

manually_written.def: 由人手工编写的；文中用来强调代码并非人工直接产出。
manually_written.eg: The team imposed a zero manually-written code constraint.
manually_written.egzh: 团队施加了零人工手写代码的约束。

acceptance_criteria.def: 判断任务是否完成、输出是否合格的一组验收标准。
acceptance_criteria.eg: Humans translated feedback into acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria.egzh: 人类把反馈转化为验收标准。

scaffold.def: 脚手架；为项目提供初始结构、规则和支撑的框架。
scaffold.egzh: Codex 生成了初始脚手架。

underspecified.def: 规定不足的；缺少足够约束和上下文，导致执行者无法可靠推进。
underspecified.eg: Early progress was slow because the environment was underspecified.
underspecified.egzh: 早期进展缓慢，是因为环境规定不足。

legible.def: 可读的；可被系统或人理解、检查和推理的。
legible.eg: The repository must be legible to Codex.
legible.egzh: 仓库必须对 Codex 可读。

enforceable.def: 可强制执行的；能通过规则、测试或工具落地的。
enforceable.eg: Architecture rules need to be enforceable.
enforceable.egzh: 架构规则需要可强制执行。

pull_request.def: 代码变更提交给仓库进行评审、验证和合并的工作单元。
pull_request.eg: Codex opened and updated pull requests.
pull_request.egzh: Codex 创建并更新 pull request。

observability.def: 可观测性；通过日志、指标和追踪理解系统运行状态的能力。
observability.eg: Observability was exposed to the agent.
observability.egzh: 可观测性能力被暴露给 Agent。

ephemeral.def: 短暂存在的；任务完成后即被销毁的。
ephemeral.eg: Each worktree used an ephemeral observability stack.
ephemeral.egzh: 每个 worktree 都使用临时可销毁的可观测性栈。

tractable.def: 可处理的；复杂问题在给定工具下变得可解决。
tractable.eg: The added context made validation prompts tractable.
tractable.egzh: 新增上下文让验证类提示变得可处理。

system_of_record.def: 权威记录系统；被视为事实来源的正式存储位置。
system_of_record.eg: The repository became the system of record.
system_of_record.egzh: 仓库成为权威记录系统。

progressive_disclosure.def: 渐进披露；先给稳定入口，再按需要引导到更深层信息。
progressive_disclosure.egzh: 渐进披露让上下文保持可管理。

monolithic.def: 单体式的；庞大且难以分解维护的。
monolithic.eg: A monolithic manual quickly became stale.
monolithic.egzh: 单体式手册很快变得陈旧。

stale.def: 陈旧的；不再反映当前事实或状态的。

invariant.def: 不变量；系统中必须始终成立的约束。
invariant.eg: The team enforced invariants instead of micromanaging code.
invariant.egzh: 团队强制执行不变量，而不是微观管理代码。

structural_test.def: 检查代码结构、依赖方向或架构边界是否合规的测试。
structural_test.egzh: 结构测试守住了依赖方向。

cross_cutting.def: 横切的；影响多个模块或领域的通用关注点。
cross_cutting.egzh: 横切关注点通过 Providers 进入。

remediation.def: 修复；针对问题给出补救步骤。
remediation.egzh: Lint 错误包含修复说明。

throughput.def: 吞吐量；单位时间内完成的工作量。
throughput.eg: Agent throughput changed the merge strategy.
throughput.egzh: Agent 吞吐量改变了合并策略。

flaky.def: 不稳定的；测试或系统时好时坏、结果不可靠。
flaky.eg: Flaky tests were often resolved by reruns.
flaky.egzh: 不稳定测试通常通过重跑处理。

autonomy.def: 自主性；系统无需持续人工干预即可推进任务的能力。
autonomy.eg: Higher autonomy required encoded validation and recovery.
autonomy.egzh: 更高自主性需要编码化的验证和恢复能力。

entropy.def: 熵；系统随时间产生混乱、漂移和衰减的趋势。

garbage_collection.def: 垃圾回收；文中借指持续、小步地清理技术债和坏模式。
garbage_collection.eg: The cleanup loop works like garbage collection.
garbage_collection.egzh: 清理循环像垃圾回收一样运作。

technical_debt.def: 技术债；为短期速度牺牲长期维护性而积累的成本。
technical_debt.egzh: 技术债如果被忽视就会复利增长。

compound.def: 复利式累积；随时间放大影响。
compound.eg: Human judgment should compound through tooling.
compound.egzh: 人类判断应通过工具复利积累。

coherent.def: 连贯一致的；内部逻辑清晰、没有互相冲突。
coherent.egzh: 代码库必须保持连贯一致。

judgment.def: 判断力；在不确定情境下作出取舍的能力。
judgment.eg: Humans step in when judgment is needed.
judgment.egzh: 需要判断力时由人类介入。

original.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world

groups.group: 引言：0 行人工手写代码的实验 · Introduction: zero manually-written code

rows.en: Over the past five months, our team has been running an experiment: building and shipping an internal beta of a software product with 0 lines of manually-written code.
rows.zh: 过去五个月，我们团队一直在做一个实验：构建并交付一个软件产品的内部 beta，而且人工手写代码为 0 行。

rows.en: The product has internal daily users and external alpha testers. It ships, deploys, breaks, and gets fixed. What's different is that every line of code--application logic, tests, CI configuration, documentation, observability, and internal tooling--has been written by Codex. We estimate that we built this in about 1/10th the time it would have taken to write the code by hand.
rows.zh: 这个产品有内部日活用户，也有外部 alpha 测试者。它会发布、部署、出故障，也会被修复。不同之处在于，每一行代码，包括应用逻辑、测试、CI 配置、文档、可观测性和内部工具，都是 Codex 写的。我们估算，相比人工手写代码，我们大约只用了十分之一的时间。

rows.en: Humans steer. Agents execute.
rows.zh: 人类掌舵，Agent 执行。

rows.en: We intentionally chose this constraint so we would build what was necessary to increase engineering velocity by orders of magnitude. We had weeks to ship what ended up being a million lines of code. To do that, we needed to understand what changes when a software engineering team's primary job is no longer to write code, but to design environments, specify intent, and build feedback loops that allow Codex agents to do reliable work.
rows.zh: 我们有意选择这个约束，是为了迫使自己构建那些真正能把工程速度提升几个数量级的东西。我们只有几周时间，却最终要交付约百万行代码。为此，我们必须理解：当一个软件工程团队的首要工作不再是写代码，而是设计环境、说明意图，并构建让 Codex Agent 能可靠工作的反馈循环时，究竟会发生什么变化。

rows.en: This post is about what we learned by building a brand new product with a team of agents--what broke, what compounded, and how to maximize our one truly scarce resource: human time and attention.
rows.zh: 这篇文章总结了我们用一组 Agent 构建全新产品时学到的东西：什么会失效，什么会复利增长，以及如何最大化利用我们真正稀缺的资源：人类时间和注意力。

groups.group: 从空 Git 仓库开始 · We started with an empty git repository

rows.en: The first commit to an empty repository landed in late August 2025.
rows.zh: 2025 年 8 月下旬，第一次提交进入了一个空仓库。

rows.en: The initial scaffold--repository structure, CI configuration, formatting rules, package manager setup, and application framework--was generated by Codex CLI using GPT-5, guided by a small set of existing templates. Even the initial AGENTS.md file that directs agents how to work in the repository was itself written by Codex.
rows.zh: 最初的脚手架，包括仓库结构、CI 配置、格式化规则、包管理器设置和应用框架，是 Codex CLI 使用 GPT-5 生成的，只由少量现有模板引导。甚至最初用于指导 Agent 如何在仓库中工作的 AGENTS.md 文件，也是 Codex 自己写的。

rows.en: There was no pre-existing human-written code to anchor the system. From the beginning, the repository was shaped by the agent.
rows.zh: 系统里没有预先存在的人工代码作为锚点。从一开始，这个仓库就是由 Agent 塑造的。

rows.en: Five months later, the repository contains on the order of a million lines of code across application logic, infrastructure, tooling, documentation, and internal developer utilities. Over that period, roughly 1,500 pull requests have been opened and merged with a small team of just three engineers driving Codex. This translates to an average throughput of 3.5 PRs per engineer per day, and surprisingly the throughput has increased as the team has grown to now seven engineers. Importantly, this wasn't output for output's sake: the product has been used by hundreds of users internally, including daily internal power users.
rows.zh: 五个月后，这个仓库已经在应用逻辑、基础设施、工具、文档和内部开发者实用程序中积累了约百万行代码。在这段时间里，一个只有三名工程师的小团队驱动 Codex，打开并合并了大约 1,500 个 pull request。折算下来，平均每名工程师每天完成 3.5 个 PR；更令人意外的是，随着团队扩大到七名工程师，吞吐量反而继续上升。重要的是，这并不是为了产出而产出：该产品已经被数百名内部用户使用，其中还包括每天重度使用的内部用户。

rows.en: Throughout the development process, humans never directly contributed any code. This became a core philosophy for the team: no manually-written code.
rows.zh: 在整个开发过程中，人类从未直接贡献任何代码。这成为团队的核心理念：不写人工手写代码。

groups.group: 重新定义工程师角色 · Redefining the role of the engineer

rows.en: The lack of hands-on human coding introduced a different kind of engineering work, focused on systems, scaffolding, and leverage.
rows.zh: 人类不再亲手编码，引入了一种不同类型的工程工作：重点转向系统、脚手架和杠杆。

rows.en: Early progress was slower than we expected, not because Codex was incapable, but because the environment was underspecified. The agent lacked the tools, abstractions, and internal structure required to make progress toward high-level goals. The primary job of our engineering team became enabling the agents to do useful work.
rows.zh: 早期进展比我们预期更慢，并不是因为 Codex 能力不足，而是因为环境规定得不够充分。Agent 缺少朝高层目标推进所需的工具、抽象和内部结构。因此，我们工程团队的首要工作变成了让 Agent 能做有用的工作。

rows.en: In practice, this meant working depth-first: breaking down larger goals into smaller building blocks (design, code, review, test, etc), prompting the agent to construct those blocks, and using them to unlock more complex tasks. When something failed, the fix was almost never "try harder." Because the only way to make progress was to get Codex to do the work, human engineers always stepped into the task and asked: "what capability is missing, and how do we make it both legible and enforceable for the agent?"
rows.zh: 在实践中，这意味着采用深度优先的工作方式：把更大的目标拆成更小的构件（设计、代码、评审、测试等），提示 Agent 构建这些构件，再用它们解锁更复杂的任务。某件事失败时，解决办法几乎从来不是“再努力一点”。因为推进工作的唯一方式是让 Codex 完成任务，所以人类工程师总会进入任务本身并追问：缺了什么能力？怎样让这种能力既能被 Agent 理解，又能被强制执行？

rows.en: Humans interact with the system almost entirely through prompts: an engineer describes a task, runs the agent, and allows it to open a pull request. To drive a PR to completion, we instruct Codex to review its own changes locally, request additional specific agent reviews both locally and in the cloud, respond to any human or agent given feedback, and iterate in a loop until all agent reviewers are satisfied. Codex uses our standard development tools directly (gh, local scripts, and repository-embedded skills) to gather context without humans copying and pasting into the CLI.
rows.zh: 人类几乎完全通过提示词与系统交互：工程师描述任务，运行 Agent，并允许它打开一个 pull request。为了推动 PR 完成，我们会指示 Codex 在本地评审自己的变更，在本地和云端请求额外的特定 Agent 评审，回应任何人类或 Agent 给出的反馈，并循环迭代，直到所有 Agent 评审者都满意。Codex 会直接使用我们的标准开发工具（gh、本地脚本和嵌入仓库的技能）收集上下文，不需要人类把内容复制粘贴到 CLI。

rows.en: Humans may review pull requests, but aren't required to. Over time, we've pushed almost all review effort towards being handled agent-to-agent.
rows.zh: 人类可以评审 pull request，但这不是必需的。随着时间推移，我们几乎把所有评审工作都推向了 Agent 与 Agent 之间完成。

groups.group: 提升应用可读性 · Increasing application legibility

rows.en: As code throughput increased, our bottleneck became human QA capacity. Because the fixed constraint has been human time and attention, we've worked to add more capabilities to the agent by making things like the application UI, logs, and app metrics themselves directly legible to Codex.
rows.zh: 随着代码吞吐量提升，我们的瓶颈变成了人类 QA 能力。由于固定约束一直是人类时间和注意力，我们开始通过让应用 UI、日志和应用指标等内容本身直接对 Codex 可读，来为 Agent 增加更多能力。

rows.en: For example, we made the app bootable per git worktree, so Codex could launch and drive one instance per change. We also wired the Chrome DevTools Protocol into the agent runtime and created skills for working with DOM snapshots, screenshots, and navigation. This enabled Codex to reproduce bugs, validate fixes, and reason about UI behavior directly.
rows.zh: 例如，我们让应用可以按每个 git worktree 单独启动，这样 Codex 就能为每个变更启动并驱动一个实例。我们还把 Chrome DevTools Protocol 接入 Agent 运行时，并创建了处理 DOM 快照、截图和导航的技能。这使 Codex 能够直接复现 bug、验证修复，并推理 UI 行为。

rows.alt: Codex browser and UI legibility workflow
rows.caption: 原文配图：通过浏览器、DOM、截图和导航能力，让 Codex 能直接复现 bug、验证修复并推理 UI 行为。

rows.en: We did the same for observability tooling. Logs, metrics, and traces are exposed to Codex via a local observability stack that's ephemeral for any given worktree. Codex works on a fully isolated version of that app--including its logs and metrics, which get torn down once that task is complete. Agents can query logs with LogQL and metrics with PromQL. With this context available, prompts like "ensure service startup completes in under 800ms" or "no span in these four critical user journeys exceeds two seconds" become tractable.
rows.zh: 我们对可观测性工具也做了同样的事。日志、指标和 trace 通过本地可观测性栈暴露给 Codex，而这个栈对任意给定 worktree 都是临时的。Codex 操作的是该应用的完全隔离版本，包括其日志和指标；任务完成后这些内容会被销毁。Agent 可以用 LogQL 查询日志，用 PromQL 查询指标。有了这些上下文，“确保服务启动在 800 毫秒内完成”或“这四条关键用户路径中没有任何 span 超过两秒”这样的提示就变得可处理。

rows.en: We regularly see single Codex runs work on a single task for upwards of six hours, often while the humans are sleeping.
rows.zh: 我们经常看到单次 Codex 运行在一个任务上工作六个多小时，而且常常发生在人类睡觉的时候。

groups.group: 仓库知识作为权威记录 · We made repository knowledge the system of record

rows.en: Context management is one of the biggest challenges in making agents effective at large and complex tasks. One of the earliest lessons we learned was simple: give Codex a map, not a 1,000-page instruction manual.
rows.zh: 要让 Agent 在大型复杂任务中有效工作，上下文管理是最大的挑战之一。我们最早学到的经验很简单：给 Codex 一张地图，而不是一本 1,000 页的说明书。

rows.en: We tried the one big AGENTS.md approach. It failed in predictable ways: context is a scarce resource; too much guidance becomes non-guidance; it rots instantly; and it is hard to verify.
rows.zh: 我们试过一个巨大的 AGENTS.md 方案。它以可预见的方式失败了：上下文是稀缺资源；过多指导会变成无效指导；它会迅速腐烂；而且很难验证。

rows.en: A monolithic manual turns into a graveyard of stale rules. Agents cannot tell what is still true, humans stop maintaining it, and the file quietly becomes an attractive nuisance.
rows.zh: 单体式手册会变成陈旧规则的墓地。Agent 分不清哪些仍然为真，人类也会停止维护它，而这个文件会悄悄变成一个看似有用、实则有害的诱因。

rows.en: So instead of treating AGENTS.md as the encyclopedia, we treat it as the table of contents.
rows.zh: 因此，我们不再把 AGENTS.md 当作百科全书，而是把它当作目录。

rows.en: The repository's knowledge base lives in a structured docs directory treated as the system of record. A short AGENTS.md, roughly 100 lines, is injected into context and serves primarily as a map, with pointers to deeper sources of truth elsewhere.
rows.zh: 仓库的知识库位于结构化的 docs 目录中，并被视为权威记录系统。一个大约 100 行的简短 AGENTS.md 会被注入上下文，它主要充当地图，指向其他位置更深层的事实来源。

rows.en: Design documentation is catalogued and indexed, including verification status and a set of core beliefs that define agent-first operating principles. Architecture documentation provides a top-level map of domains and package layering. A quality document grades each product domain and architectural layer, tracking gaps over time.
rows.zh: 设计文档会被编目和索引，其中包括验证状态，以及一组定义 Agent-first 操作原则的核心信念。架构文档提供领域和包分层的顶层地图。质量文档则为每个产品领域和架构层评分，并持续跟踪缺口。

rows.en: Plans are treated as first-class artifacts. Ephemeral lightweight plans are used for small changes, while complex work is captured in execution plans with progress and decision logs that are checked into the repository. Active plans, completed plans, and known technical debt are all versioned and co-located, allowing agents to operate without relying on external context.
rows.zh: 计划被视为一等产物。小变更使用临时的轻量计划；复杂工作则记录在执行计划中，包含进度和决策日志，并提交到仓库。活跃计划、已完成计划和已知技术债都会被版本化并放在同一处，使 Agent 不依赖外部上下文也能工作。

rows.en: This enables progressive disclosure: agents start with a small, stable entry point and are taught where to look next, rather than being overwhelmed up front.
rows.zh: 这实现了渐进披露：Agent 从一个小而稳定的入口开始，并被教会下一步该去哪里查找，而不是一开始就被大量信息淹没。

rows.en: We enforce this mechanically. Dedicated linters and CI jobs validate that the knowledge base is up to date, cross-linked, and structured correctly. A recurring doc-gardening agent scans for stale or obsolete documentation that does not reflect the real code behavior and opens fix-up pull requests.
rows.zh: 我们用机械化方式强制执行这一点。专门的 linter 和 CI 任务会验证知识库是否保持最新、是否交叉链接、结构是否正确。一个周期性运行的“文档园艺”Agent 会扫描那些陈旧或过时、已经不能反映真实代码行为的文档，并打开修复型 pull request。

groups.group: Agent 可读性是目标 · Agent legibility is the goal

rows.en: As the codebase evolved, Codex's framework for design decisions needed to evolve, too.
rows.zh: 随着代码库演进，Codex 用来做设计决策的框架也必须随之演进。

rows.en: Because the repository is entirely agent-generated, it's optimized first for Codex's legibility. In the same way teams aim to improve navigability of their code for new engineering hires, our human engineers' goal was making it possible for an agent to reason about the full business domain directly from the repository itself.
rows.zh: 由于这个仓库完全由 Agent 生成，它首先针对 Codex 的可读性进行优化。就像团队会努力让新入职工程师更容易浏览代码一样，我们的人类工程师目标是让 Agent 能够直接从仓库本身推理完整业务领域。

rows.en: From the agent's point of view, anything it can't access in-context while running effectively doesn't exist. Knowledge that lives in Google Docs, chat threads, or people's heads are not accessible to the system. Repository-local, versioned artifacts, such as code, markdown, schemas, and executable plans, are all it can see.
rows.zh: 从 Agent 的视角看，运行时无法在上下文中访问的东西，实际上就不存在。存在于 Google Docs、聊天线程或人脑中的知识，系统都访问不到。它能看到的只有仓库本地、带版本的产物，例如代码、Markdown、schema 和可执行计划。

rows.caption: 原文配图：只有仓库本地、版本化且运行时可访问的上下文，才真正对 Agent 可见。

rows.en: Giving Codex more context means organizing and exposing the right information so the agent can reason over it, rather than overwhelming it with ad-hoc instructions. In the same way you would onboard a new teammate on product principles, engineering norms, and team culture, giving the agent this information leads to better-aligned output.
rows.zh: 给 Codex 更多上下文，并不是用临时指令淹没它，而是组织并暴露正确的信息，让 Agent 能基于这些信息推理。就像你会向新同事介绍产品原则、工程规范和团队文化一样，向 Agent 提供这些信息会带来更对齐的输出。

rows.en: This framing clarified many tradeoffs. We favored dependencies and abstractions that could be fully internalized and reasoned about in-repo. Technologies often described as boring tend to be easier for agents to model due to composability, API stability, and representation in the training set. In some cases, it was cheaper to have the agent reimplement subsets of functionality than to work around opaque upstream behavior from public libraries.
rows.zh: 这种框架澄清了许多取舍。我们偏好那些可以在仓库内被完全内化、并可被推理的依赖和抽象。那些常被称为“无聊”的技术，由于可组合性、API 稳定性以及在训练集中的表达，往往更容易被 Agent 建模。在某些情况下，让 Agent 重新实现部分功能，甚至比绕开公共库中不透明的上游行为更便宜。

rows.en: Pulling more of the system into a form the agent can inspect, validate, and modify directly increases leverage--not just for Codex, but for other agents working on the codebase as well.
rows.zh: 把系统中更多部分转化为 Agent 可以直接检查、验证和修改的形式，会提高杠杆效应；受益的不只是 Codex，也包括其他在这个代码库上工作的 Agent。

groups.group: 用规则守住架构和品味 · Enforcing architecture and taste

rows.en: Documentation alone doesn't keep a fully agent-generated codebase coherent. By enforcing invariants, not micromanaging implementations, we let agents ship fast without undermining the foundation.
rows.zh: 仅靠文档无法让一个完全由 Agent 生成的代码库保持一致。我们通过强制执行不变量，而不是微观管理具体实现，让 Agent 能快速交付，同时不破坏基础。

rows.en: Agents are most effective in environments with strict boundaries and predictable structure, so we built the application around a rigid architectural model. Each business domain is divided into a fixed set of layers, with strictly validated dependency directions and a limited set of permissible edges. These constraints are enforced mechanically via custom linters and structural tests.
rows.zh: Agent 在边界严格、结构可预测的环境中最有效，所以我们围绕一个刚性的架构模型构建应用。每个业务领域被划分为固定层级，依赖方向经过严格验证，可允许的连接边也受到限制。这些约束通过自定义 linter 和结构测试进行机械化执行。

rows.en: Within each business domain, code can only depend forward through a fixed set of layers. Cross-cutting concerns such as auth, connectors, telemetry, and feature flags enter through a single explicit interface: Providers. Anything else is disallowed and enforced mechanically.
rows.zh: 在每个业务领域内，代码只能沿固定层级向前依赖。认证、连接器、遥测、功能开关等横切关注点，则通过唯一明确的接口 Providers 进入。其他路径都不允许，并由机械化规则强制执行。

rows.alt: Layered domain architecture with Providers boundary
rows.caption: 原文配图：业务领域只能沿固定层级向前依赖，横切关注点通过 Providers 这一明确边界进入。

rows.en: This is the kind of architecture you usually postpone until you have hundreds of engineers. With coding agents, it's an early prerequisite: the constraints are what allows speed without decay or architectural drift.
rows.zh: 这种架构通常会被推迟到团队拥有数百名工程师之后才做。但在编码 Agent 场景下，它是早期前提：正是这些约束让速度不会带来衰减或架构漂移。

rows.en: In practice, we enforce these rules with custom linters and structural tests, plus a small set of taste invariants. Because the lints are custom, we write the error messages to inject remediation instructions into agent context.
rows.zh: 实践中，我们用自定义 linter、结构测试，以及一小组“品味不变量”来执行这些规则。由于 lint 是自定义的，我们会把错误信息写成可注入 Agent 上下文的修复说明。

rows.en: In a human-first workflow, these rules might feel pedantic or constraining. With agents, they become multipliers: once encoded, they apply everywhere at once.
rows.zh: 在人类优先的工作流中，这些规则可能显得吹毛求疵或过于束缚。但在 Agent 场景下，它们会成为倍增器：一旦被编码，就会同时作用于所有地方。

rows.en: Human taste continuously feeds back into the system. Review comments, refactoring pull requests, and user-facing bugs are captured as documentation updates or encoded directly into tooling. When documentation is insufficient, rules become code.
rows.zh: 人类品味会持续反馈进系统。评审评论、重构 pull request 和面向用户的 bug，会被记录为文档更新，或直接编码进工具。当文档不足以约束行为时，规则就会变成代码。

groups.group: 吞吐量改变合并哲学 · Throughput changes the merge philosophy

rows.en: As Codex throughput increased, many traditional engineering norms stopped working.
rows.zh: 随着 Codex 吞吐量提升，许多传统工程规范开始失效。

rows.en: The repository minimizes blocking merge gates during operation. Pull request lifetimes are short. Flaky tests are often resolved by follow-up reruns rather than blocking progress indefinitely. In a system where agent throughput far exceeds human attention, correction is cheap and waiting is expensive.
rows.zh: 这个仓库在运行过程中尽量减少阻塞式合并门禁。Pull request 生命周期很短。不稳定测试通常通过后续重跑解决，而不是无限期阻塞进展。在一个 Agent 吞吐量远超人类注意力的系统里，修正很便宜，等待很昂贵。

rows.en: In a low-throughput environment, this would be irresponsible. Here, it is often the correct choice.
rows.zh: 在低吞吐环境中，这样做会不负责任。但在这里，它往往是正确选择。

groups.group: 什么才算 Agent 生成 · What agent-generated actually means

rows.en: When we say the codebase is generated by Codex agents, we mean the entire codebase.
rows.zh: 当我们说代码库由 Codex Agent 生成时，指的是整个代码库。

rows.en: Agent output includes product code and tests, CI configuration and release tooling, internal developer tools, documentation and design history, evaluation frameworks, review comments and replies, scripts that manage the repository itself, and production dashboard definitions.
rows.zh: Agent 的输出包括产品代码和测试、CI 配置和发布工具、内部开发者工具、文档和设计历史、评估框架、评审评论与回复、管理仓库本身的脚本，以及生产仪表盘定义。

rows.en: Humans are always involved, but the abstraction level of the work is different. We prioritize work, translate user feedback into acceptance criteria, and validate outcomes. When agents struggle, we treat it as a signal: identify what is missing--tools, guidance and constraints, documentation--and feed that back into the repository, with Codex writing the fixes itself.
rows.zh: 人类始终参与其中，但工作抽象层级不同。我们负责确定优先级，把用户反馈转化为验收标准，并验证结果。当 Agent 遇到困难时，我们把它视为一个信号：识别缺少什么——工具、指导和约束、文档——再把这些反馈进仓库，由 Codex 自己写出修复。

rows.en: Agents can use our standard development tools directly. They pull review feedback, reply inline, push updates, and often squash and merge their own pull requests.
rows.zh: Agent 可以直接使用我们的标准开发工具。它们会拉取评审反馈、在线回复、推送更新，并且常常自己 squash 并合并 pull request。

groups.group: 自主性水平提升 · Increasing levels of autonomy

rows.en: Increasing levels of autonomy
rows.zh: 自主性水平提升

rows.en: As more and more parts of development were encoded directly into the system--testing, validation, review, feedback handling, and recovery--the repository recently crossed an important threshold: Codex can now drive a new feature end to end.
rows.zh: 随着越来越多开发环节被直接编码进系统，包括测试、验证、评审、反馈处理和恢复，这个仓库最近跨过了一个重要门槛：Codex 现在可以端到端推动一个新功能。

rows.en: Given a prompt, the agent can verify the current state of the codebase, reproduce a reported bug, record a video demonstrating the failure, implement the fix, validate the fix by running the application, record a second video demonstrating the solution, open a pull request, respond to agent and human feedback, detect and repair build failures, hand off to a human only when judgment is needed, and merge the change.
rows.zh: 给定一个提示后，Agent 可以验证代码库当前状态，复现报告的 bug，录制展示失败的视频，实现修复，通过运行应用验证修复，再录制展示解决方案的视频，打开 pull request，回应 Agent 和人类反馈，检测并修复构建失败，只在需要判断力时交接给人类，并最终合并变更。

rows.en: This behavior depends heavily on the specific structure and tooling of this repository and should not be assumed to generalize without similar investment--at least not yet.
rows.zh: 这种行为高度依赖该仓库的具体结构和工具投入。如果没有类似投入，不应假定它可以直接泛化，至少现在还不能。

groups.group: 熵与垃圾回收 · Entropy and garbage collection

rows.en: Entropy and garbage collection
rows.zh: 熵与垃圾回收

rows.en: Fully autonomous agents also introduce new problems. Codex reproduces patterns that already exist in the repository--including uneven or undesirable ones. Over time, this inevitably creates drift.
rows.zh: 完全自主的 Agent 也会引入新问题。Codex 会复现仓库中已经存在的模式，包括不均衡或不理想的模式。久而久之，这不可避免地会产生漂移。

rows.en: At first, humans handled this manually. Our team used to spend Fridays--20% of the week--cleaning up AI slop. Unsurprisingly, that did not scale.
rows.zh: 起初，人类手动处理这个问题。我们团队过去会花掉每周的周五，也就是 20% 的时间，清理 AI 产出的劣质内容。不出所料，这种方式无法扩展。

rows.en: Instead, we began encoding what we call golden principles directly into the repository and built a recurring cleanup loop. These principles are opinionated mechanical rules designed to keep the codebase legible and consistent for future agent runs.
rows.zh: 于是，我们开始把所谓“黄金原则”直接编码进仓库，并构建一个周期性清理循环。这些原则是带有明确立场的机械规则，用来让代码库在未来 Agent 运行时仍保持可读和一致。

rows.en: We regularly run background Codex tasks that scan for drift, update quality grades, and open targeted refactoring pull requests. Most of these can be reviewed in under a minute and auto-merged.
rows.zh: 我们会定期运行后台 Codex 任务，扫描漂移、更新质量评分，并打开有针对性的重构 pull request。大多数这类 PR 可以在一分钟内完成评审并自动合并。

rows.en: It works like garbage collection. Technical debt is a high-interest loan: paying it down continuously in small amounts is better than letting it compound and resolving it painfully all at once. Once human taste is captured, it applies continuously to every line of code.
rows.zh: 它的工作方式类似垃圾回收。技术债是一种高息贷款：持续小额偿还，胜过任其复利增长后再一次性痛苦清偿。一旦人类品味被捕获，它就会持续作用于每一行代码。

groups.group: 仍在学习什么 · What we are still learning

rows.en: So far, this strategy has worked well for internal release and adoption at OpenAI. Building a real product for real users has anchored our investments in reality and pushed us toward long-term maintainability.
rows.zh: 到目前为止，这一策略在 OpenAI 内部发布和采用中运行良好。为真实用户构建真实产品，让我们的投入扎根于现实，并推动我们走向长期可维护性。

rows.en: What we do not yet know is how architectural coherence evolves over time in a fully agent-generated system. We are still learning where human judgment matters most and how to encode that judgment so it compounds. We also do not know how this system will evolve as model capabilities improve over time.
rows.zh: 我们尚不清楚的是，在一个完全由 Agent 生成的系统中，架构一致性会如何随时间演化。我们仍在学习人类判断力最重要的位置，以及如何把这种判断力编码下来，让它产生复利效应。我们也不知道随着模型能力不断提升，这个系统会如何演进。

rows.en: What is clear is that building software still requires discipline, but the discipline now lives more in the support structure than in the code. The tools, abstractions, and feedback loops that keep the codebase coherent matter more than ever.
rows.zh: 明确的是，构建软件仍然需要纪律；只是这种纪律现在更多存在于支撑结构中，而不是代码本身。让代码库保持一致的工具、抽象和反馈循环，比以往任何时候都更重要。

footer.sourceText: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
